title: Christmas Dinner
timelineNote: Times assume Thursday, Dec 24, a 6:00 pm sit-down, a 15–16 lb frozen turkey and your one convection oven. Use convection for the carrots, and regular bake for everything else, since the recipes are written that way.

items.text: Buy a frozen turkey, 15–16 lb
items.note: Any time you have freezer space. Thawing starts Sunday morning, Dec 20.

items.text: Test-fit the oven
items.note: Roasting pan on the bottom rack with a second rack above it. Check that a 13×9 dish and two sheet pans fit. This decides how much can share the oven with the turkey.

items.text: Plan fridge space
items.note: A 15–16 lb turkey needs a full shelf. Overflow can go in the cold garage only if it stays below 4°C, so check it with a thermometer. Keep the thawing turkey and anything with meat, dairy or eggs in the fridge. Drinks, produce and the cranberry sauce are fine in the garage.

items.text: Buy pantry items and equipment
items.note: Flour, sugars, yeast, stock, spices, foil, parchment, twine.

items.text: Buy dried bread cubes for the stuffing
items.note: Unseasoned, about 12 cups (14 oz).

items.text: Charge the Bluetooth thermometer and check the probe
Move the frozen turkey to the fridge
items.note: Allow 24 hours for every 4–5 lb, so 3–4 days for 15–16 lb. Sunday morning gives it about 4 days. Leave it wrapped, on a tray on the bottom shelf.

items.text: Buy produce, butter, milk, cream, sour cream and eggs
Buy fresh herbs
Make the cranberry sauce
items.note: Boil 1 cup water with 1¼ cups sugar, add the cranberries, return to a boil, then cover and simmer about 15 minutes until very thick. Off the heat, stir in cinnamon, nutmeg and orange zest and press the berries to break them up. Use a high-sided pot (they splatter). Keeps 7 days in the fridge.

items.text: Check the turkey has thawed
items.note: Press the thickest part of the thigh. It should give a little. Still hard? See “If the turkey is still icy” at the bottom.

items.text: Yams, around 2:00 pm: bake the candied yams
items.note: Oven to 375°F. Slice the yams, coat them in the melted butter, sugar and spice mix, and spread in a deep 13×9 dish covered tightly with foil. In at 2:30 for 45 minutes covered, then stir and bake 45 more uncovered, until very tender. Out about 4:00. Cool 30 minutes, cover and refrigerate. The oven is free all day on the 23rd, and this is done well before the roll dough at 5:30.

items.text: Rolls, around 5:30 pm: make both batches of dough, one after the other
items.note: About 15 minutes each in the stand mixer. Cover and let them rise until doubled, 1–2 hours.

items.text: Rolls, around 7:30 pm: shape and refrigerate
items.note: 14–16 balls per batch in a greased 9×13 pan. Cover tightly and refrigerate. Sally allows up to about 15 hours, so don't shape them earlier than this.

items.text: Simmer the neck and giblets for the gravy
items.note: From the turkey cavity. Bring to a boil in water, simmer about 1 hour. Keep the liquid. Pick the neck meat, dice it with the heart and gizzard (discard the liver), and refrigerate both.

items.text: Prep vegetables
items.note: Peel the carrots and cut large ones into 1½-inch pieces. Chop onions and celery for the stuffing.

items.text: Make the vinaigrette and toast the walnuts
items.note: Shake in a jar: ¾ cup olive oil, 6 tbsp apple cider vinegar, 2 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp Dijon, 3 small minced garlic cloves, 3 generous pinches each of salt and pepper. Refrigerate. Toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring, then cool and store airtight.

items.text: Trim and blanch the green beans
items.note: Boil in two batches, 4 minutes each, in a large pot of water with 4 tsp salt. Rinse under cold tap water, shake dry and refrigerate in a towel-lined container.

items.text: Lay out dishes, pans, serving bowls and utensils
Set the table
Stuffing: brown the sausage, sauté the vegetables, mix with bread, herbs, stock and eggs
items.note: Add the stock slowly. Stop when the bread is moist but not soggy. You may need up to 1 more cup, since bought cubes are drier and there are no mushrooms.

items.text: Rolls out of the fridge. Keep them covered and let them rise on the counter
items.note: 1–2 hours, until puffy. They go in the oven at 12:15.

items.text: Stuffing into the oven at 350°F
items.note: Turn the oven on to 350°F at 10:10. Covered for 25 minutes, then uncovered for about 20.

items.text: Roast the carrots at 425°F on convection
items.note: Toss with 3½ tbsp olive oil, 1¾ tsp kosher salt and ½ tsp pepper. One layer over two parchment-lined sheet pans. 20–25 minutes, swapping the pans halfway, until a fork goes in with a little resistance. They finish cooking in the reheat.

items.text: Whip the herb butter
items.note: 5–7 minutes in the stand mixer, then mix in herbs, garlic, salt and pepper.

items.text: Carrots out. Rolls in at 350°F, both pans, 20–25 minutes
items.note: Regular bake, not convection. Open the oven door for a minute so it drops from 425°F. Use two racks and swap the pans halfway. Rolls must be out by 12:40, before the oven goes to 450°F for the turkey. Cool, then cover tightly.

items.text: Cool the stuffing and carrots for 30 minutes, cover, and move to the fridge
items.note: They are reheated from cold later.

items.text: Prep the turkey
items.note: Pat dry. Stuff the cavity with lemon, parsley and bay leaves. Butter under the skin on the breast and back. Truss.

items.text: Oven to 450°F
Turkey in: bottom rack, breast up, 450°F for 22–25 minutes
items.note: Until browned on top.

items.text: Flip the turkey breast down, cover the top with bacon, oven to 350°F
items.note: Very hot. Gloves, towels and a second person.

items.text: Mashed potatoes: slow-cook the garlic in olive oil
items.note: ½ cup + 2 tbsp olive oil and 5 peeled garlic cloves in a small pot on low, 20–30 minutes, until golden and soft. Strain, keeping the garlic and the oil, and leave both out until 5:00.

items.text: Remove the bacon and return the turkey to the oven
Peel and quarter 5 lb Yukon Gold potatoes and cover them with cold water
Start watching the thermometer
items.note: 9–11 minutes per lb after the flip puts the finish at roughly 3:55–4:35. Pull at 165°F in the thickest part.

items.text: Put a big pot of salted water on to boil for the potatoes
items.note: It takes about 20 minutes to come to a boil.

items.text: Turkey out. Rest on the board, loosely covered in foil
items.note: Billy rests it 15–20 minutes. Wrapped fully in foil or in a cooler it holds up to 90 minutes.

items.text: Gravy: pour the pan drippings into the fat separator and skim most of the fat
items.note: Whisk 1 cup drippings with ½ cup flour over medium heat until golden. Add 4 cups stock and 1 more cup drippings, whisk 5–8 minutes until thick, then stir in the giblets. Thin with giblet liquid. Taste before salting, since the bacon makes the drippings salty. Keep warm on low.

items.text: Potatoes and 14 garlic cloves into the boiling water, 10–12 minutes
items.note: Warm the cream and butter in a small pot at the same time.

items.text: Mash the potatoes with the boiled garlic. Fold in the cream and butter, the slow-cooked garlic and its oil, and the sour cream
items.note: Add three-quarters of each first, then the rest to taste. Season with salt and white pepper. Keep covered on very low heat, stirring now and then.

items.text: Carve the turkey
items.note: A job for your helper.

items.text: Reheat the stuffing (splash of stock) and yams, covered, at 350°F for 25–30 minutes, until hot
items.note: Leave a rack free for the carrots, which go in at 5:35. Everything comes out together at 5:55.

items.text: Carrots in, uncovered, for 15–20 minutes
items.note: Reheat on one pan next to the stuffing and yams. At 5:55 taste for salt, add pepper and sprinkle with parsley.

items.text: Sauté the green beans in two batches
items.note: Large skillet, medium-high, 2 tbsp olive oil per batch. Add the beans and 4 minced garlic cloves together and toss 2–3 minutes, until the garlic is golden and the beans are hot. Season with salt and pepper. Optional: lemon zest and a squeeze of juice. Take the beans out of the fridge at 5:00.

items.text: Warm the rolls
items.note: Air fryer on low for a few minutes, checking often.

items.text: Assemble the apple spinach salad
items.note: Take the vinaigrette out of the fridge at 5:00 and shake it. Slice the red onion and rinse it in cold water. Slice the apples now, not earlier, so they don't brown. Toss the spinach, apples, onion, walnuts, cranberries and half the goat cheese with the dressing, then top with the rest of the goat cheese. A good job for a helper.

items.text: Gravy, cranberry sauce and everything to the table
items.note: Top the mashed potatoes with melted butter and chives.

items.text: Sit down

lines.label: Size
lines.text: 15–16 lb (recipe is for 12–14 lb)

lines.label: Method
lines.text: 450°F for 22–25 min, flip, 350°F for 9–11 min per lb. Done at 165°F.

lines.label: Notes
lines.text: Herb butter under the skin, bacon on top. Rests 15–20 min, holds up to 90.

recipe.title: The juiciest roast turkey
recipe.time: Prep 30 min · roast about 2½–3¼ hr · rest 20 min

ingredients.name: turkey
ingredients.note: 15–16 lb, thawed, neck and giblets removed for the gravy

steps.t: Whip {butter} butter in a stand mixer for 5 to 7 minutes, until light and fluffy.

steps: Mix in {parsley} parsley, {thyme} thyme, {rosemary} rosemary, {sage} sage, {garlic} garlic cloves, {salt} sea salt and {pepper} black pepper.

steps.t: Pat {turkey} turkey completely dry with paper towels, inside and out.

steps: Stuff the cavity with {lemon} halved lemon, a handful of parsley sprigs and {bay} bay leaves.
Gently loosen the skin over the breast and the back with your fingers. Spread the herb butter evenly underneath the skin. Close any tears with toothpicks.
Truss the legs and wings with butcher's twine.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the bottom position.
Set the turkey breast side up on the rack in the roasting pan. Roast 22 to 25 minutes, until browned on top.
Carefully flip the turkey breast side down. It is very hot, so use gloves, towels and a helper. Lay {bacon} bacon strips over the top and lower the oven to 350°F.
Remove the bacon so the back can brown, and keep roasting.
Roast 9 to 11 minutes per pound in total after the flip, about 2¼ to 3 hours for this size. Pull it when the thickest part of the breast or thigh reads 165°F.
Rest loosely covered with foil for 15 to 20 minutes. Wrapped fully in foil or in a cooler it holds up to 90 minutes.

steps: Remove the twine, the toothpicks and the cavity aromatics, then carve.
notes: Billy's recipe is written for a 12–14 lb bird. The herb butter stays the same for 15–16 lb; only the roasting time grows.
Roast on the bottom rack so heat circulates and the bottom doesn't steam.
Thaw in the fridge, 24 hours for every 4–5 lb. This plan starts it Sunday morning, Dec 20.
Leftovers keep 5 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Reheat covered at 350°F with ½–1 cup stock for 15–20 minutes.

lines.label: Size
lines.text: One batch (recipe serves 15)

lines.label: Method
lines.text: Pan drippings roux (1 cup drippings, ½ cup flour), 4 cups stock plus 1 more cup drippings, diced giblets. About 15 minutes while the turkey rests.

lines.label: Make ahead
lines.text: Simmer the neck and giblets the day before. Short on drippings? Top up with 1–2 tbsp butter and a little stock.

recipe.title: Turkey gravy
recipe.time: Giblets 1 hr the day before · gravy 20 min

ingredients.name: turkey neck, heart and gizzard
ingredients.note: from the turkey; discard the liver

steps.t: Put the neck, heart and gizzard in a pot and cover with water. Bring to a boil, then simmer about 1 hour.

steps: Strain, keeping the liquid. Pick the meat off the neck and dice it with the heart and gizzard. Refrigerate the meat and the liquid separately.

steps.t: Pour the pan drippings into a fat separator or a large bowl. Let the fat rise and skim most of it off.

steps: In a saucepan over medium heat, whisk {drippings:1/2} drippings with {flour} flour into a smooth paste. If it looks greasy, add a little more flour. Cook, whisking, until golden brown.
Whisk in {stock} chicken stock and {drippings:rest} drippings. Keep whisking 5 to 8 minutes, until thickened.
Stir in the diced giblet meat.
Too thick? Thin it with the giblet liquid. Too thin? Simmer 10 minutes more, then whisk in {corn} cornstarch mixed with {water} cold water.
Taste first, then season with salt and pepper. The bacon makes the drippings salty. Keep warm on low until 5:55.
notes: Short on drippings? Top up with 1–2 tbsp butter and a little more stock.
Leftovers keep 2–3 days. Reheat with a splash of stock over medium-low for about 15 minutes.

lines.label: Size
lines.text: One batch (recipe serves 10)

lines.label: Method
lines.text: Simmer cranberries with sugar and water about 15 min, finish with orange zest, cinnamon and nutmeg. Chill 30–45 min.

lines.label: Make ahead
lines.text: Up to 2 days ahead (keeps 7 days in the fridge, or freezes for 3 months).

recipe.title: Cranberry sauce
recipe.time: Prep 5 min · cook 20 min · chill 45 min

steps.t: In a high-sided medium pot, bring {water} water and {sugar} sugar to a full boil.

steps: Add {cranberries} cranberries and bring back to a boil, until they start to pop.
Cover and simmer about 15 minutes, until very thick. Add a splash of water if the pot looks dry.
Off the heat, stir in {cinnamon} cinnamon, {nutmeg} nutmeg and the zest of {orange} orange, pressing the berries to break them up.
Move to a container and refrigerate until cold, at least 30 to 45 minutes.
notes: Keeps 7 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. It thickens and tastes better cold.

lines.label: Size
lines.text: One batch (recipe serves 16), made without the mushrooms

lines.label: Method
lines.text: 350°F, 25 min covered, about 20 uncovered

lines.label: Make ahead
lines.text: Keeps 4 days. Reheat at 350°F for 15–20 min with ¼–⅓ cup stock.

recipe.title: Traditional stuffing

steps.t: Melt {butter:1/2} butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown {sausage} sausage, breaking it up, until cooked through. Lift it out of the pan.

steps: Melt {butter:rest} butter in the same pan and cook {onion} onions for 4 to 5 minutes.
Add {celery} celery stalks and {garlic} garlic cloves and cook 4 to 5 minutes, until the celery is tender.
Put the vegetables, sausage and dried bread cubes in a large bowl.
Gently mix in {sage} sage, {rosemary} rosemary, {thyme} thyme, and salt and pepper.
Pour in {stock} chicken stock a little at a time, mixing gently. Stop once the bread is moist but not soggy. Bought cubes and no mushrooms make it drier, so you may need up to 1 more cup.
Stir in {eggs} whisked eggs.
Spread in a 13×9-inch baking dish and cover with foil.

steps.t: Bake at 350°F for 25 minutes. Uncover and bake about 20 minutes more, until lightly browned on top.
Cool 30 minutes, cover and refrigerate until the reheat.
Reheat covered at 350°F with a splash of stock for 25 to 30 minutes, until hot. Garnish with chopped parsley.

notes: Made without the 2 cups of cremini mushrooms in Billy's recipe, so the mushroom step is left out.
Uses store-bought dried bread cubes, so there's no drying step.
Taste the mixture before the eggs go in and adjust the seasoning.
Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen.

lines.label: Size
lines.text: 1.5× (recipe serves 8)

lines.label: Method
lines.text: 375°F: 45 min covered, stir, then 45 min uncovered.

lines.label: Make ahead
lines.text: Baked on Dec 23 and reheated on the day. Keeps 5 days. Does not freeze well.

recipe.title: Candied yams

steps.t: Heat the oven to 375°F. Put {yams} sliced yams in a large bowl.

steps: In a medium pot over low heat, melt {butter} butter with {sugar} brown sugar, {vanilla} vanilla, {cinnamon} cinnamon, {nutmeg} nutmeg and a pinch of salt. Whisk until smooth.
Pour the mixture over the yams and toss until every slice is coated.
Spread in a deep 13×9-inch baking dish and cover tightly with foil. This much is a lot for one dish, so use a deep one or split it between two.

steps.t: Bake covered for 45 minutes.
Take off the foil and stir.

steps: Bake uncovered for another 45 minutes, until very tender.

steps.t: Cool 30 minutes, cover and refrigerate until the next day.
On Dec 24, reheat covered at 350°F for 25 to 30 minutes, until hot.

notes: Follows Billy's recipe card: 45 minutes covered, stir, then 45 minutes uncovered. A full 1.5× batch may need a few extra minutes, so check that the slices are very tender.
Made the day before, on Dec 23. Keeps 5 days in the fridge. Does not freeze well.

lines.label: Size
lines.text: 1.25× (recipe serves 8), 5 lb Yukon Golds

lines.label: Method
lines.text: Garlic slow-cooked in olive oil on the stove, potatoes boiled with more garlic, then mashed with cream, butter, garlic oil and sour cream. No oven needed.

lines.label: Make ahead
lines.text: Garlic oil any time that afternoon. The mash holds up to 1 hour, covered on very low heat.

recipe.title: Roasted garlic mashed potatoes

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: all of it goes into the mash

ingredients.name: coarse salt and ground white pepper

steps.t: Put {oil} olive oil and {garlic} peeled garlic cloves in a small pot. Cook over low heat for 20 to 30 minutes, until the garlic is lightly browned and soft. Strain, keeping both the garlic and the oil. Leave them at room temperature until you mash.
Peel and quarter {potatoes} Yukon Gold potatoes. Cover them with cold water until it's time to boil.
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. It takes about 20 minutes.
Drain the potatoes, add them to the boiling water with {garlic2} garlic cloves, and cook at a low boil for 10 to 12 minutes, until a fork slides in easily. Don't overcook them.

steps: Meanwhile, warm {cream} heavy cream and {butter} butter in a small pot over low heat until the butter melts.

steps.t: Drain the potatoes and mash them with the boiled garlic until smooth, using a masher, hand mixer, stand mixer or food mill.

steps: With a spatula, fold in the hot cream and butter, the slow-cooked garlic and its oil, {sourcream} sour cream, and salt and white pepper. Add about three-quarters of each first, then the rest as needed.
Cover and keep warm over very low heat, stirring now and then, for up to 1 hour.

steps.t: Serve topped with {butter2} melted butter and chives.

notes: Billy's recipe serves 8, so everything is 1.25×. The garlic oil uses your amounts, ½ cup oil and 4 cloves before scaling, instead of Billy's 1½ cups and ½ cup.
Too thick? Stir in a little more warm cream or sour cream.
Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Reheat in a pot over low heat with a little butter or milk.

lines.label: Size
lines.text: 2¼ lb (1 kg) for 10, 4× the recipe

lines.label: Ingredients
lines.text: Salt for the blanching water. ¼ cup olive oil, 8 garlic cloves finely minced, ½ tsp salt, pepper.

lines.label: Method
lines.text: Blanch 4 min on Wed Dec 23, rinse under cold water, dry and chill. At 5:35, sauté with the garlic in two batches, 2–3 min each.

recipe.title: Garlic sautéed green beans
recipe.time: Blanch 10 min on Wed Dec 23 · sauté 6 min

ingredients.name: garlic cloves
ingredients.note: finely minced with a knife, not a press

steps.t: Bring a large pot of water to a boil with {bsalt} salt.

steps: Add half of the {beans} green beans and cook 4 minutes, until bright green. Lift them out, then cook the other half the same way.
Drain, rinse under cold tap water to cool, and shake off the excess water. Ice water isn't needed.
Dry well and refrigerate in a towel-lined container.

steps.t: Heat {oil:1/2} olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.

steps: Add half the beans and {garlic:1/2} garlic cloves. Toss for 2 to 3 minutes, until the garlic is golden and crispy and the beans are hot.
Add {salt:1/2} salt and a couple of pinches of pepper, toss, and move to a serving dish.
Repeat with {oil:rest} olive oil, the rest of the beans, {garlic:rest} garlic cloves, and the rest of the salt and pepper. Serve warm.
Optional: finish with the zest of {lemon} lemon and a squeeze of its juice.
notes: Nagi's recipe is 250 g, which serves 2 to 4. 4× gives about 100 g each for 10.
Take the beans out of the fridge at 5:00 so they aren't icy when they hit the pan. The recipe's sauté is only 2 minutes, so allow up to 3 when they start cold.
Mince the garlic with a knife. A press makes it wet, so it spits and burns.

lines.label: Size
lines.text: 3½ lb carrots for 10 (1.75× the recipe, which serves 6)

lines.label: Ingredients
lines.text: 3½ tbsp olive oil, 1¾ tsp kosher salt, about ½ tsp black pepper, parsley to garnish. No sweetener.

lines.label: Method
lines.text: Roast at 425°F on convection for 20–25 min at midday on two pans, chill, then reheat uncovered at 350°F for 15–20 min from 5:35.

recipe.title: Easy oven roasted carrots
recipe.time: Roast 20–25 min at midday · reheat 15–20 min

ingredients.name: carrots
ingredients.note: peeled, large ones cut into 1½-inch pieces

steps.t: Heat the oven to 425°F on convection. Line two sheet pans with parchment.

steps: Toss {carrots} carrots with {oil} olive oil, {salt} kosher salt and {pepper} black pepper.
Spread them in one layer over the two pans, with space between the pieces.
Roast 20 to 25 minutes, swapping the pans halfway. Take them out when a fork goes in with a little resistance. They finish cooking in the reheat.

steps.t: Cool 30 minutes, combine onto one pan, cover and refrigerate.
Reheat uncovered at 350°F for 15 to 20 minutes, next to the stuffing and yams, until a fork goes in easily.
Taste for salt, add more pepper and sprinkle with parsley.

notes: Spend With Pennies serves 6 from 2 lb, so everything is 1.75× (rounded up a little for 10).
Roasted on convection, so it takes 20–25 minutes instead of the card's 25–30 for store-bought carrots.
No honey or sugar, since the candied yams are already sweet.

lines.label: Size
lines.text: Two separate batches, 28–32 rolls (Sally advises against doubling)

lines.label: Method
lines.text: 350°F for 20–25 min on a lower rack

lines.label: Make ahead
lines.text: Shape on the evening of Dec 23 and refrigerate overnight. Out of the fridge at 10:15, bake at 12:15, warm just before dinner.

recipe.title: Soft dinner rolls
recipe.servings: Makes 14–16 rolls per batch. Make two batches.
recipe.time: Prep 25 min · rising about 3 hr · bake 22 min

steps.t: Whisk {milk} warm milk, {yeast} instant yeast and {sugar:1 tbsp} sugar together. Let stand 5 minutes.

steps: Add {sugar:rest} sugar, {egg} egg, {butter} softened butter, {salt} salt and {flour:1 cup} flour. Mix on low speed.
Add {flour:rest} flour and mix on medium until the dough pulls away from the sides of the bowl. Only if it is too sticky, add more flour a tablespoon at a time.
Knead 5 minutes by mixer or by hand, until soft and slightly tacky. A poke should spring back slowly.
Put the dough in a greased bowl, turn it to coat, cover and let it rise 1 to 2 hours, until doubled.
Grease a 9×13-inch pan.

steps.t: Punch down the dough. Divide it into 14 to 16 pieces and shape each into a smooth ball. Arrange them in the pan.

steps: Cover tightly and refrigerate overnight, up to about 15 hours.

steps.t: Take the pans out, keep them covered, and let the rolls rise on the counter 1–2 hours, until puffy.

steps: When the carrots come out, let the oven drop to 350°F, with a rack in a lower position.

steps.t: Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until golden, turning the pan halfway. Tent with foil if the tops brown too fast.

steps: Optional: brush with {butter2} melted butter mixed with {honey} honey. Cool, then cover tightly.

steps.t: Warm the rolls in the air fryer on low for a few minutes, checking often. Or reheat covered at 300°F for about 10 minutes.

notes: Amounts are for one batch. Sally advises against doubling, so make the batch twice.
Shaped the evening before and refrigerated, as Sally's notes allow, then baked at midday while the oven is free.

recipe.title: Apple spinach salad
recipe.time: Dressing 5 min on Wed Dec 23 · assemble 10 min

ingredients.name: small apples
ingredients.note: cored and thinly sliced; a mix of sweet Pink Lady and tart Granny Smith

steps.t: Whisk or shake {oil} olive oil, {vinegar} apple cider vinegar, {honey} honey, {dijon} Dijon, {garlic} minced garlic cloves and 3 generous pinches each of salt and pepper in a jar. Refrigerate.

steps: Toast {walnuts} chopped walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring. Cool, then store airtight.

steps.t: Take the dressing out of the fridge so it loosens, and shake it.
Thinly slice 1½ small red onions and rinse in cold water to mellow them. Drain well.

steps: Core and thinly slice {apples} apples. Do it now, not earlier, so they don't brown.
In a large bowl, combine {spinach} baby spinach, the apples, onion, walnuts, {cran} dried cranberries and {goat:1/2} goat cheese.
Drizzle with the vinaigrette and toss.
Top with {goat:rest} goat cheese and serve right away.
notes: The recipe doesn't list servings. 3× uses 15 oz of spinach, the same amount planned before for 10.
No cooking on the day, so this is a good job for a helper.

callouts.title: If the turkey is late.
callouts.text: Leave it in until it reads 165°F. The sides do not reheat until 5:25, so there is slack. If it is still in at 5:15, give it a short 15-minute rest and warm the sides in the microwave in portions.

callouts.title: If the turkey is still icy.
callouts.text: On the morning of the 24th, keep it in its wrapper and put it breast down in a sink of cold water. Change the water every 30 minutes and allow about 30 minutes per pound that is still frozen.

callouts.title: For a lighter day.
callouts.text: Bake the stuffing, yams and carrots on Wed Dec 23 and reheat them from the fridge on the day.
